results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $a$ and $b$, the Gibonacci generating function $G^{(a,b)}(x) = \frac{(b - a)x + a}{1 - x - x^2}$ takes the value $G^{(a,b)}(0) = a$ at $x = 0$.

results.title: Value of the Gibonacci generating function at one

results.title: Goodness passes to two transformed fractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary:
Let $a$, $b$, $p$, $q$ be integers with $q 
e 0$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$, and suppose that $p/q$ is good for $(a, b)$. If $p + q 
e 0$, then $q/(p + q)$ is good for $(a, b)$; and if $p 
e 0$, then $(q - p)/p$ is good for $(a, b)$.

results.title: Congruence criterion for good fractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a, b, p, q$ be integers with $(a, b) \ne (0, 0)$, $q \ne 0$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$, and put $m = |q^2 - pq - p^2|$. Then $p / q$ is good for $(a, b)$ if and only if there are integers $u$ and $v$ with $(q - p) u \equiv 1$, $p v \equiv 1$, $a \equiv -b p u$ and $a \equiv -b q v \pmod{m}$.

results.title: Consecutive Fibonacci ratios are good
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $a$ and $b$ and every natural number $n$, the ratio $F_n / F_{n+1}$ of consecutive Fibonacci numbers is good for $(a, b)$.

results.title: Two standard families of good values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be integers and let $(G_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Gibonacci sequence with $G_0 = a$ and $G_1 = b$. For every natural number $n$, the ratio $F_n / F_{n+1}$ of consecutive Fibonacci numbers is good for $(a, b)$, and if $G_n \ne 0$, then $-G_{n+1} / G_n$ is good for $(a, b)$.

results.title: Generating function of the recurrence $A_{n+1} = pA_n + A_{n-1}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For integers $a$, $b$, $p$ and a rational number $x$, $A(x) = \frac{a(1 - px) + bx}{1 - px - x^2}$, with the convention that a fraction with denominator $0$ is $0$. As a rational function, $A$ is the generating function $\sum_{n \ge 0} A_n x^n$ of the sequence with $A_0 = a$, $A_1 = b$ and $A_{n+1} = pA_n + A_{n-1}$; for $p \ne 0$ the denominator $1 - px - x^2$ has no rational root.

results.title: Value of the generating function at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $a, b, p$, the function $A(x) = \frac{a(1 - px) + bx}{1 - px - x^2}$ on the rationals satisfies $A(0) = a$.

results.title: Forward part of a second-order sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For integers $p, r, s$, this is the sequence $(A^{(r,s)}_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of integers with $A^{(r,s)}_0 = r$, $A^{(r,s)}_1 = s$ and $A^{(r,s)}_{n+2} = pA^{(r,s)}_{n+1} + A^{(r,s)}_n$ for every natural number $n$.

results.title: Backward part of the two-sided sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For integers $p$, $r$ and $s$, the backward part is the sequence $(B_k)_{k \ge 0}$ with $B_0 = s$, $B_1 = r$ and $B_{k+2} = B_k - pB_{k+1}$. Thus $B_k$ is the term of index $1 - k$ of the two-sided sequence with $A_0 = r$, $A_1 = s$ and $A_{n+1} = pA_n + A_{n-1}$, computed backwards by $A_n = A_{n+2} - pA_{n+1}$.

results.title: Two-sided second-order sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For integers $p$, $r$ and $s$, the two-sided sequence $(A^{(r,s)}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ for $p$ is the integer sequence indexed by $\mathbb{Z}$ with $A^{(r,s)}_0 = r$, $A^{(r,s)}_1 = s$ and $A^{(r,s)}_{n+1} = pA^{(r,s)}_n + A^{(r,s)}_{n-1}$ for every integer $n$.

results.title: First values of the two-sided sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $p$, $r$, $s$, the two-sided sequence $(A^{(r,s)}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ for $p$ with initial values $r$ and $s$ satisfies $A^{(r,s)}_0 = r$, $A^{(r,s)}_1 = s$, $A^{(r,s)}_2 = ps + r$ and $A^{(r,s)}_{-1} = s - pr$.

results.title: First initial value of the two-sided sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $p$, $r$, $s$, the two-sided sequence $(A^{(r,s)}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ for $p$ with initial values $r$ and $s$ satisfies $A^{(r,s)}_0 = r$.

results.title: Second initial value of the two-sided sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $p$, $r$, $s$, the two-sided sequence $(A^{(r,s)}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ for $p$ with initial values $r$ and $s$ satisfies $A^{(r,s)}_1 = s$.

results.title: The two-sided sequence satisfies its recurrence at every index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$, $r$, $s$ be integers and $(A^{(r,s)}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ the two-sided sequence for $p$ with initial values $A^{(r,s)}_0 = r$ and $A^{(r,s)}_1 = s$. Then $A^{(r,s)}_{n+2} = pA^{(r,s)}_{n+1} + A^{(r,s)}_n$ for every integer $n$.

results.title: The quantity $M(r, s)$ for the recurrence $A_{n+1} = pA_n + A_{n-1}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For integers $a$, $b$, $p$, $r$, $s$, $M(r, s) = \frac{br^2 + bs^2 - apr^2 + 2ars}{s^2 - prs - r^2}$, a rational number, with the convention that a fraction with denominator $0$ is $0$.

results.title: Relations between values of $M$ at neighbouring pairs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $p$ be integers with $p \ne 0$, and for integers $r$, $s$ let $M(r, s) = \frac{br^2 + bs^2 - apr^2 + 2ars}{s^2 - prs - r^2}$. Then for all integers $r$, $s$ that are not both zero, $M(s - pr, r) + (p^2 + 2)M(r, s) + M(s, r + ps) = 0$ and $M(r, s)^2 + (p^2 + 2)M(r, s)M(s, r + ps) + M(s, r + ps)^2 = abp^3 + (a^2 - b^2)p^2$.

results.title: Rationals where $x/(1 - px - x^2)$ is an integer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p \ne 0$ be an integer, let $G(x) = \frac{x}{1 - px - x^2}$ for rational $x$, and let $A^{(0,1)}$ be the two-sided integer sequence with $A^{(0,1)}_0 = 0$, $A^{(0,1)}_1 = 1$ and $A^{(0,1)}_{n+2} = pA^{(0,1)}_{n+1} + A^{(0,1)}_n$ for all integers $n$. Then the set of rational numbers $x$ for which $G(x)$ is an integer is $\{A^{(0,1)}_n / A^{(0,1)}_{n+1} : n \in \mathbb{Z},\ n \ne -1\}$.

results.title: Integer values of $x/(1 - px - x^2)$ come from Lucas ratios
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p \ne 0$ be an integer, let $(U_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Lucas sequence $U(p, -1)$, so $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = pU_{n+1} + U_n$, and let $G(x) = \frac{x}{1 - px - x^2}$ for rational $x$. Then $G(U_n/U_{n+1})$ is an integer for every natural number $n$; and if $G(x) = k$ for a rational number $x$ and an integer $k$, then $G(U_n/U_{n+1}) = k$ for some natural number $n$.

results.title: Strictly decreasing tuples

results.title: Empty strictly decreasing tuple

results.title: Multiple zeta summand
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbf{k} = (k_0, \dots, k_{r-1})$ be an index of depth $r$ and let $(m_0, \dots, m_{r-1})$ be a strictly decreasing $r$-tuple of positive integers. The summand attached to $\mathbf{k}$ and this tuple is the real number $\left(\prod_{i=0}^{r-1} m_i^{k_i}\right)^{-1}$.

results.title: Empty weakly decreasing tuple

results.title: Multiple-zeta-star summand

results.title: Star and strict summands agree on strictly decreasing tuples

results.title: Weak-star polar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real topological vector space $E$ and a subset $s \subseteq E$, the weak-star polar of $s$ is the set of continuous linear functionals $\varphi$ on $E$, viewed as elements of the weak dual of $E$, such that $|\varphi(x)| \le 1$ for every $x \in s$.

results.title: Banach–Alaoglu–Bourbaki theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real locally convex topological vector space and let $U$ be a neighbourhood of $0$ in $E$. Then the weak-star polar of $U$ is compact in the weak dual of $E$, that is, in the space of continuous linear functionals on $E$ with the weak-star topology.

results.title: Finite-dimensional bicommutant theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S$ be a unital $*$-subalgebra of the algebra $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of complex $n \times n$ matrices. Then the commutant of the commutant of $S$ equals $S$: a matrix commutes with every matrix that commutes with all elements of $S$ if and only if it lies in $S$.

results.title: Probability of quartet split 03|12 on the caterpillar tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the caterpillar species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `03 | 12` has probability `(1/3) e^{-y}`.

results.title: No anomalous unrooted quartets, balanced species tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: No anomalous unrooted quartets, balanced species tree (Allman, Degnan & Rhodes 2011): on `((0, 1), (2, 3))` the unrooted gene quartet matches `01 | 23` with probability `1 - (2/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`, where `y₁ + y₂` is the internal edge of the unrooted species quartet.

results.title: Probability of quartet split 02|13 on the balanced tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the balanced species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `02 | 13` has probability `(1/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`.

results.title: Probability of quartet split 03|12 on the balanced tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the balanced species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `03 | 12` has probability `(1/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`.

results.title: The species quartet maximizes quartet support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The species quartet maximizes quartet support (Allman, Degnan & Rhodes 2011; Mirarab et al. 2014): for a positive internal edge, the unrooted gene quartet matching the species quartet is strictly the most probable of the three, on both four-species shapes. Since the expected quartet support of a candidate four-species tree (one quartet) is the probability of its quartet, the species tree maximizes it.

results.title: Clade of a ranked history
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The set `S` of sampled genes is a clade of the ranked history `h`: it is a block of one of the ancestral partitions of `h`, i.e. the set of descendants of some lineage.

results.title: Clade probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Clade probability (Rosenberg 2003): under random joining, a fixed set of `k` among `m` genes, `1 ≤ k < m`, is a clade with probability `2m / (k (k + 1) C(m, k))`.

results.title: Clade probability under random joining for at most five genes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The case `m ≤ 5` of `randomJoining_isClade`.

results.title: Single-input single-output linear time-invariant system
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A single-input single-output linear time-invariant system `ẋ = A x + u b`, `y = c ⬝ x + d u` with state space `n → ℝ`.

results.title: Vector field of a linear time-invariant system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The vector field `A x + u b` at state `x` and input `u`.

results.title: Output of a linear time-invariant system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The output `c ⬝ x + d u`, measured from its adapted value.

results.title: Perfect adaptation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every constant input `u`, the output vanishes at every equilibrium.

results.title: Integral feedback
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A linear functional `z = k ⬝ x` of the state integrates the output, `ż = k ⬝ (A x + u b) = y`, for every state and input.

results.title: Steady-state (DC) gain of a linear system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The steady-state (DC) gain `d - c ⬝ A⁻¹ b`; for nonsingular `A` the output at the equilibrium for input `u` is `dcGain * u`.

results.title: Integral feedback implies perfect adaptation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Integral feedback implies perfect adaptation.

results.title: Unique equilibrium of a nonsingular linear system
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonsingular `A`, the unique equilibrium for input `u` is `x = -u • A⁻¹ b`.

results.title: Output at equilibrium equals DC gain times input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonsingular `A`, the output at the equilibrium for input `u` is `dcGain * u`.

results.title: Perfect adaptation iff the DC gain vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonsingular `A`, perfect adaptation holds iff the steady-state gain vanishes.

results.title: Integral feedback is necessary
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Integral feedback is necessary (linear systems with nonsingular `A`): perfect adaptation holds iff some linear functional of the state integrates the output; one such functional is `k = c A⁻¹`.

results.title: Integral-feedback functional is the time integral of the output
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Along a trajectory `ẋ(t) = A x(t) + u(t) b`, the functional `k ⬝ x(t)` of an integral-feedback system has derivative `y(t) = c ⬝ x(t) + d u(t)`: it is the time integral of the output.

results.title: Integral feedback gives robust perfect adaptation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Integral feedback gives robust perfect adaptation (nonlinear form). Let `F p` be the vector field and `y p` the output of a system with parameters `p`, and let `z` be a differentiable state function with derivative `z' x` satisfying `z' x (F p x) = y p x` for all `p`, `x` (so `ż = y` along every trajectory, for every parameter). Then the output vanishes at every equilibrium of every `F p`.
